God for his passion, what make you here alone, I lookd for you at my lodge an hower agoe, what meanes your compa ny to leaue you thus? who brought you hither? M. Clare. Whoes that? M. Ierningham, you are a couple of hot shots, does a man commit his wench to you, to put her to grasse at this time of night? Seeking for stealers are abroad to night, My hound staied on her, and so found her out. Which way tooke they? A plague vpon't, thats that damned Priest, & Blague of the George, he that serues the good Duke of Norfolke. Zownds you suspected them, and now they are heere indeed. If you goe to the lodge you are surely taken, Strike downe the wood to Enfeild presently, And if Mounchensey come, Ile send him t'yee: Let mee alone to bussle with your father, I warrant you that I will keepe them play, Till you haue quit the chase: away, away. Whoes there? Stand or Ile shoote. I am the keeper that doe charge you stand, You haue stollen my D •••• You are arrant theeues, and ye haue stolne my Deere. The more your shame that Knights should bee such thieues. My name is Brian, keeper of this walke. You haue stolne the best Deere in my walke to night, my Deere. What make you in my walke? you haue stolne the best Bucke in my walke to night. My Deere. Wheres my Bucke. Ile complaine vnto the King you spoile his game: Tis strange that men of your account and calling, will offer it, I tell you true, Sir Arthur and sir Raph, that none but you haue onely spoild my game. I charge you both ye get out of my ground. Is this a time for such as you, men of place and of your grauity, to be abroad a theeuing! tis a shame, and a fore God if I had shot at you, I had serude you well enough.
I heard one speake here hard by in the bottome; peace Maister, speake low, zownes if I did not heare a bow goe off, and the Bucke bray, I neuer heard deere in my life.
An hower a goe. I will Sir.
In the kings name pursue the Rauisher. We are Knights, sir Arthur Clare and sir Raph Ier ningham. O Brian a villain, Thou hast receiued my daughter to thy lodge. Where is Mountchensey? Good morrow gentle knight, A happy day after your short nights rest, Did not you tell vs still how Peter Fabell at length would crosse vs if we tooke not heed? Did not you send your nouice Benedic, To perswade the girle to leaue Mountchenseys loue, To crosse that Peter Fabell in his art, And to that purpose made him visitor? Did not I direct you to the house? Confer with you from Waltham Abby Vnto Chesson wall? Why knaue, didst thou not tell me an hower ago mine host was vp? Why, who's thy Master? is not the Master of the house thy Master? We haue bin in the Forrest all night almost. How I married! If any law in England will make thee smart for this, expect it with all seuerity. Did we not last night find two S. Georges here.
Heeres a sky as blacke as Luciser, God blesse vs, heere was goodman Theophilus buried, hee was the best Nutcraker that euer dwelt in Enfeild: well, tis 9. a clock, tis time to ring cur few. Lord blesse vs, what a white thing is that in the Church porch; O Lorde my legges are too weake for my body, my haire is too stiffe for my night-cap, my heart failes; this is the ghost of Theophilus, O Lord it followes me, I cannot say my prayers and one would giue me a thousand pound: good spirit, I haue bowld and drunke and followed the hounds with you a thousand times, though I haue not the spirit now to deale with you; O Lord. We are grasse and hay indeede; I know you to bee Master Parson by your phrase. I Sir. O Lord I am a man of another element; Maister Theophilus Ghost is in the Church porch, there was a hundred Cats all fire dancing here euen now; and they are clombe vp to the top of the steeple, ile not into the bellfree for a world. It may be a womans body Sir Iohn.
Grasse and hey, we are all mortall, who's there? Sexton. For mortalities sake, What's the matter? O good Salomon; I haue bin about a deede of darknes to night: O Lord I saw fifteen spirits in the forrest, like white bulles, if I lye I am an arrant theefe: mortalitie haunts vs; grasse and hay the deuills at our heeles, and lets hence to the parso nages.
By the Lord there are some watchmen; I heare them name Maister Constable, I would to God my Mill were an Eunuch and wanted her stones, so I were hence.
Tis the Constable by this light, Ile steale hence, and if I can meete mine host Blague, ile tell him how Smug is taine, and will him to looke to him selfe.
O no mine host, but there sate one in the porch, I haue not breath ynough left to blesse me from the Deuill.
Good morrow reuerend Knights vnto you both. Alas good knights, how might the matter be? Let mee vnderstand your greefe for Charity. A holy woman, benedicite; now God forfend that any should presume to touch the sister of a holy house. Was that faire maiden late become a Nun! It is the First time that I ere heard of it. Why Reuerend knight? Nay then giue me leaue sir to depart in quiet, I had hopd you had sent for mee to some other end. Sir Arthur, by my order and my faith, I know not what you meane. Yes that I am: I neuer heard of any match intended. The more I striue to know what you should meane, the lesse I vnderstand you. I haue heard of one that is a great magician, But hees about the Vniuersity. I neuer sent my nouice from the house, Nor haue we made our visitation yet. That you shall know, hee came along with me, and stayes without come hither Benedic. Yong Benedic, were you ere sent by me to Chesson Nunnery for a visitor?
Neuer sir, truely. I neuer saw you sir before this hower.
I sir, my Master's vp. I sir, my M. is vp, but I thinke M. Blague indeed be not stirring? Yes sir, but M. Blague dwells ouer the way. S foote our signes remooud, this is strange.
